bands.label: Exemplar
bands.blurb: Reference-quality API operations across every facet.

providers.name: Salla
providers.description: Salla is a Saudi Arabia-based e-commerce platform — often called the Shopify of the Middle East — that lets merchants launch, operate, and grow Arabic-first online stores without code. Founded in 2016 in Makkah by Nawaf Hariri and Salman Butt, Salla now powers more than 80,000 active stores. The platform exposes a Merchant REST API (https://api.salla.dev/admin/v2), an OAuth 2.0 Partners authorization service, signed webhooks for the full storefront lifecycle, a Shipping and Fulfillment app contract, the Twilight theme engine and JavaScript SDK, the Salla CLI, and official starter kits for PHP/Laravel and Node.js/Express. Backed by Sanabil (PIF), STV, Investcorp, Vision Ventures, and Raed Ventures, Salla raised a $130M pre-IPO round in 2024.

providers.name: PayTabs
providers.description: PayTabs is a Saudi-built payment orchestration and gateway provider serving merchants across MENA. The PT2 REST API accepts cards and local methods (mada, Meeza, KNET, OmanNet, Benefit, STC Pay, urpay) plus Apple Pay, Google Pay and Samsung Pay through hosted, managed and own-form flows, with tokenization, recurring billing and invoicing. The API is served on region-specific hosts and authenticated with a merchant server key.

bands.label: Strong
bands.blurb: Solid contracts, transparent operations, and an easy start.

providers.name: Paymob
providers.description: Paymob is a Cairo-headquartered, licensed payment infrastructure provider for the MENAP region. Serving roughly 390,000 merchants across Egypt, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Oman, and Pakistan (with Qatar announced), Paymob unifies card acquiring, regional mobile wallets (Vodafone Cash, Etisalat Cash, Orange Money, STC Pay, Oman Net, EasyPaisa, JazzCash), BNPL rails (Tabby, Tamara, valU, Souhoola, Forsa, Aman), Apple Pay, Google Pay, POS terminals, subscriptions, installments, marketplace payouts, mass disbursement (Paymob Send), and an end-to-end cashless commerce platform (Paymob Sync) behind a single Accept / Intentions API surface.

providers.name: Tamara
providers.description: Tamara is the Saudi Arabia–headquartered MENA shopping and Buy-Now-Pay-Later platform offering Shariah-compliant split-payment and Pay-Now solutions across Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Oman. Founded in 2020 and licensed by SAMA (Saudi Central Bank), Tamara provides merchants with a hosted-checkout Direct API, in-store SMS and QR payment links, mobile SDKs for iOS, Android, Flutter, and React Native, plug-and-play e-commerce extensions for Shopify, Magento, OpenCart, PrestaShop, Salesforce Commerce Cloud and WooCommerce, webhooks for order and dispute lifecycle events, and a Channel Partners onboarding API for payment service providers and platforms that white-label Tamara. The company became the first homegrown Saudi fintech unicorn in December 2023 after raising a US$340M Series C led by SNB Capital and Sanabil Investments and is backed by debt facilities from Goldman Sachs, Citi, and Apollo for its Shariah-compliant funding base.

providers.name: Lean Technologies
providers.description: Lean Technologies is a MENA open finance and payments infrastructure platform serving the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. Its APIs let businesses connect to customers' bank accounts to read financial data (accounts, balances, transactions, identity, income and credit insights) and to move money via pay-by-bank payments, Account-on-File consents, payment links, payouts, refunds and scheduled payments. Lean provides the LinkSDK client for web, iOS, Android, React Native and Flutter, a FAPI-grade OAuth 2.0 authorization server, webhooks, a hosted documentation MCP server, and public Postman collections. Lean is regulated under the UAE Open Finance (CBUAE) and Saudi Open Banking (SAMA) frameworks and is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified.

providers.name: Unifonic
providers.description: Unifonic is a Saudi Arabia-based customer engagement and CPaaS platform, backed by SoftBank Vision Fund, that powers SMS, WhatsApp, voice, push notification, and OTP-verification communication for enterprises across the Middle East and beyond. Its developer surface spans an SMS (NextGen) REST API, an Authenticate API for multi-channel OTP verification, Voice APIs for calls, IVR, and number masking, and a WhatsApp Conversations API with template, session, and management endpoints, alongside webhooks for delivery status and channel events, mobile push SDKs, a web event-tracking SDK, chatbot and Flow Studio automation products, and a WhatsApp sandbox for testing.

providers.name: HyperPay
providers.description: HyperPay is a MENA / Saudi Arabia online payment gateway built on the ACI / OPPWA Open Payment Platform. Its REST API powers the COPYandPAY hosted widget and a Server-to-Server integration, accepting cards (VISA, MASTER, AMEX), the Saudi domestic mada scheme, STC Pay, and Apple Pay, priced and settled in SAR. Additional products include HyperSplit (marketplace payouts) and HyperBill (invoicing).

bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: Lean Technologies
providers.description: Lean Technologies is a Middle East Open Banking and Open Finance infrastructure provider founded in 2019 and headquartered in the UAE. Lean offers regulated Account Information (AIS), Payment Initiation (PIS), payouts, refunds, account and name verifications, and derived insights across the UAE and Saudi Arabia, with verification coverage extending to 27+ countries globally. Lean holds an In-Principle Approval from the Central Bank of UAE for Open Finance Services (August 2025), a Major Payment Institution licence from the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA), and an FSP licence from the Abu Dhabi Global Market FSRA (no. 200033). The platform is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022 certified and has processed AED 16B+ across 2M+ linked accounts. Investors include Sequoia, General Catalyst, Breyer Capital, Shorooq, Raed, BCV, and Liberty City.

providers.name: Tabby
providers.description: Tabby is the MENA region's largest buy-now-pay-later (BNPL) provider, founded in 2019 by Hosam Arab (ex-Namshi) and Daniil Barkalov, originally in Dubai and now headquartered in Riyadh ahead of a planned IPO. Tabby reached a $3.3B valuation in a February 2025 Series E ($160M co-led by Blue Pool Capital and Hassana Investment Company), making it the most valuable fintech in the Middle East, and reports 15M+ users, 40,000+ merchants, and $10B+ in annualized transaction volume across KSA, UAE, and Kuwait. The Tabby API powers split-purchase checkouts (Pay-in-4 interest-free, monthly plans up to 12 months), payment lifecycle management, webhooks, and dispute resolution, complemented by Tabby Card (Visa-enabled), Tabby Shop discovery, Tabby Care purchase protection, and the Tabby Plus loyalty programme. Public developer surface includes a versioned REST API across two regional hosts (api.tabby.ai for UAE/Kuwait, api.tabby.sa for KSA), an OpenAPI 3.1 specification, iOS / Android / Flutter / React Native SDKs, and certified Magento 2, Shopify, WooCommerce, Salla, Zid, OpenCart, ExpandCart, Matjrah, Salesforce, and Odoo plugins.

providers.name: EdfaPay, Inc.
providers.description: EdfaPay is a Saudi fintech and payment-technology company offering a developer-friendly payment platform across the GCC region. Its products include a hosted Checkout and Server-to-Server (S2S) payment gateway, SoftPOS tap-to-pay technology that turns mobile devices into card readers, merchant onboarding, payouts, e-invoicing, and white-label solutions for banks and partners. The gateway supports Visa, Mastercard, MADA, Apple Pay and STC Pay with 3D Secure, webhooks, refunds and recurring payments, on PCI-DSS certified infrastructure. EdfaPay was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched from its public developer documentation, OpenAPI definitions and SDKs.

providers.name: Spare
providers.description: Spare is a MENA-region open banking and open finance platform, licensed by the Central Bank of Bahrain as an Account Information Service Provider and Payment Initiation Service Provider (AISP/PISP) and permitted to test under the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) regulatory sandbox. Spare exposes RESTful Account Information Services (AIS) — account details, balances, transactions, statements, beneficiaries, parties, direct debits, plus risk and affordability reports — and Payment Initiation Services (PIS) for domestic single, future-dated and standing-order payments, across separate Bahrain, KSA and UAE tenants hosted in-region for data-residency compliance. Developers authenticate with OAuth2 client credentials to obtain signed JWT bearer tokens, drive a customer to connection to consent to data flow, verify token and webhook signatures against a published JWKS, and integrate via official TypeScript, Java, .NET and PHP SDKs plus Postman collections.

providers.name: OTO Global
providers.description: OTO is a multi-carrier shipping and fulfillment platform for e-commerce businesses, headquartered in Saudi Arabia and serving 10,000+ merchants. It connects a single integration to 450+ shipping carriers and provides order management, warehouse and picking/packing automation, real-time tracking with customer notifications, returns management, address validation, and omnichannel order synchronization. The OTO REST API V2 (base https://api.tryoto.com/rest/v2, staging at staging-api.tryoto.com) exposes 74 operations across orders, shipments, returns, tracking, shipping rates, carrier integrations, pickup locations, products, stock management, sales channels, and webhooks. Authentication is a bearer access_token minted from a dashboard refresh_token.

providers.name: Sadq Holding Limited
providers.description: Sadq (صادق) is a Saudi Arabian electronic-signature and digital-trust platform that lets businesses send, sign, and manage legally binding documents online. Its Integration API covers signing envelopes and document packages, signing invitations (email/SMS/link), direct and template-based signing, PKI/e-signing via Saudi Arabia's Nafath national digital identity, document download, reusable templates, users and permissions, signing workflows, webhooks, KYB business verification (commercial-registration checks, Absher OTP, delegacy and national-address lookups), archiving, delegations, and consumption reporting. The platform is fully agent-native — it publishes an OpenAPI schema, an RFC 9727 API catalog, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC discovery metadata, an llms.txt, an auth.md agent-registration guide, and a hosted MCP server. Sadq is a 500 Global portfolio company.

providers.name: Oumla Ltd
providers.description: Oumla is a Saudi-based provider of enterprise-grade digital asset infrastructure for regulated institutions. Its Core API delivers MPC-based wallet and address management, portfolio and native-balance queries, on-chain transaction tracking, smart-contract templates plus deployment and read/write interactions, and tokenization (collections, issue, mint, burn) for tokenized securities, fund units, sukuk, and NFTs. Products span Digital Assets Infrastructure (custody, policy engines, lifecycle), Capital Markets Tokenization, the Oumla Financial Chain for Shariah-compliant interbank settlement, and Bahith blockchain monitoring and compliance analytics built for Saudi data sovereignty. Authentication is via the x-api-key header; long-running mutations run as async workflows. Oumla is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified.

providers.name: Reachware Inc.
providers.description: Reachware is an Integration Platform as a Service (iPaaS) that lets separate SaaS and business systems operate as one connected ecosystem, with 200+ prebuilt connectors to systems like NetSuite, QuickBooks, Microsoft Dynamics 365, Odoo, SAP, Oracle, Magento, Zid and Qoyod. Alongside the core platform it ships Reach Pay (a payment API for Saudi Arabia payment gateways), Reachware Fatoora (ZATCA e-invoicing), and extension modules for banking, HR, inventory, loyalty and property management. Reach Pay exposes a hosted-redirect REST API for requesting payments, retrieving payment details, refunds and card tokenization. Reachware reports 3,500+ active subscriptions, 300+ customers, 100M+ transactions, and is CMMI Level 3 certified. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and profiled by the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline.

providers.name: Sarj AI Developer API
providers.description: Sarj.ai is a voice and chat AI agent platform built for Arabic, English and Urdu, focused on the Saudi and wider MENA market. The public developer surface is a REST API for outbound voice calls — place a call against a saved scenario, then retrieve its status, signed recording URL, transcript and asynchronous post-call outcome report. Alongside the call API, Sarj publishes two OpenAI-compatible speech APIs (Speech-to-Text with streaming, and Text-to-Speech with voice cloning), a hosted MCP server exposing createCall and getCall as native agent tools, an A2A agent card, a published Agent Skill, an llms.txt, webhook push notifications for call completion, and an official Python SDK.

providers.name: King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals
providers.description: King Fahd University of Petroleum & Minerals (KFUPM) is a public research university in Dhahran, Saudi Arabia, ranked #101 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. KFUPM does not operate a centralized public developer portal, but several institutional systems expose machine-readable interfaces: the KFUPM ePrints theses and dissertations repository serves a live OAI-PMH 2.0 endpoint and EPrints REST URLs, and the Elsevier Pure research portal (pure.kfupm.edu.sa) ships the standard Pure Web Services REST API (OpenAPI 3, authentication-gated). KFUPM also maintains a GitHub organization and a student Open Source Club presence.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Labayh
providers.description: Labayh (لبيه) is a Saudi Arabian digital mental-health platform delivering online psychological, psychiatric and family counselling to the Arabic-speaking Gulf market. Patients book scheduled or instant video and audio sessions with more than 1,000 licensed specialists, and can also enrol in structured therapeutic programs for depression, anxiety, OCD and social phobia, join peer support groups, take psychological assessments, track mood daily, and watch live and recorded webinars. The company reports over 70 million minutes of consultation delivered. Alongside the consumer app it runs Labayh Business, a corporate employee-wellbeing arm, and Labayh Academy, a training platform for practitioners. Labayh is backed by 500 Global. It operates no developer program and publishes no OpenAPI, SDKs or developer portal; the API catalogued here is the anonymously readable WordPress REST surface behind labayh.net, whose OpenAPI description API Evangelist derived from the server's own discovery document.

providers.name: Taker
providers.description: Taker is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia-based restaurant technology company (founded 2018, backed by 500 Global) providing an all-in-one online ordering and restaurant-growth platform used by 1,000+ restaurants. Its product suite spans Taker Channels (branded web/mobile ordering), Taker GO (delivery operations), Taker Flow (operations optimization), Taker Grow (marketing automation), and Taker 360 (a unified dashboard across delivery aggregators). The Taker GO delivery-integration API connects restaurants and delivery service providers (DSPs) with bearer-token auth for order creation, tracking, cancellation, and asynchronous status delivery via webhooks, across published sandbox and production environments.

providers.name: Moyasar
providers.description: Moyasar is a Saudi Arabian payment gateway that lets businesses accept online payments across mada, Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Apple Pay, Samsung Pay, and STC Pay. Its REST API (base https://api.moyasar.com/v1) covers payments (create, fetch, list, refund, capture, void), hosted invoices, card tokenization, webhooks, and payouts / disbursements. Authentication is HTTP Basic with a publishable or secret API key as the username and an empty password, in separate test and live modes.

providers.name: Abwab Ai
providers.description: Abwab.ai is an AI-powered credit intelligence platform for MSME (micro, small, and medium enterprise) lending, used by banks, NBFIs, fintechs, funds, and digital platforms to originate loans, assess credit risk, price, and monitor MSME loan portfolios across the full lending lifecycle. The platform combines rules and AI models for real-time credit decisioning, agentic credit intelligence that surfaces leads and flags portfolio risk, and embedded financing for existing SME platforms. It is API-first, plugging into existing loan-origination and core-banking systems without core replacement, with a versioned REST API (api.abwab.ai), webhook notifications, and Python/Node.js SDKs in development. Abwab is focused on the Saudi Arabian market with in-Kingdom data residency and alignment to the SAMA Cybersecurity Framework, PDPL, and Sharia-compliant lending (used by Kafalah). Backed by Speedinvest.

providers.name: Geidea
providers.description: Geidea is a Saudi-headquartered fintech and payments platform serving merchants across the MENA region (Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and the UAE). Its Payment Gateway lets merchants accept card and wallet payments through a hosted Geidea Checkout (HPP) page or a server-to-server Direct API for PCI-DSS-compliant merchants, covering the full transaction lifecycle - create session, 3-D Secure authentication, pay, capture, void, refund, cancel, tokenization, Pay by Link, and Pay by Invoice - with support for mada, Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Meeza QR, and BNPL. Payments are authenticated with a merchant public key and API password over HTTP Basic auth plus an HMAC request signature, and results are delivered back to merchants via webhook (callback) notifications.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: Lendo
providers.description: Lendo (شركة ليندو السعودية للتمويل) is a Riyadh-based Saudi fintech licensed by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA, License No. 61/A SH/202203, capital SAR 50M) that operates the Kingdom's first SAMA-licensed Sharia-compliant debt-based crowdfunding platform. Lendo connects small and medium enterprises needing liquidity with retail and institutional investors, offering invoice financing, working capital financing, purchase-order financing and term loans funded within 48 hours of document completion, alongside government-backed programs with Monshaat, SME Bank, the Tourism Development Fund, the Cultural Development Fund, Modon and the Kafala guarantee scheme. On the investor side it runs tiered retail products (Basic, Premium, High Net Worth), an auto-invest engine and an A-D credit scoring engine, reporting SAR 4.5B+ in cumulative financing across 10,000+ funded deals at a 2.93% overall default rate. Lendo publishes no public developer program, API documentation or SDKs; its production API host is authentication-gated and its machine-readable public surface is limited to an llms.txt and a SafeBase-hosted trust center.

providers.name: Karaz Platform
providers.description: Karaz is an AI-driven Electronic Health Record (EHR) platform based in Saudi Arabia that connects healthcare practitioners, patients, insurance providers, and wellness vendors in a unified health-management ecosystem. It provides real-time biometric and continuous-glucose (CGM) monitoring, AI-driven treatment insights, patient and provider mobile apps, analytics and reporting, rewards and community engagement, and a health-vendor marketplace, with integrations across Apple, Abbott, Medtronic, Dexcom, Roche, Google, and Omron. The Karaz developer API (early-stage) exposes Karaz App and Karaz Care resources over HTTPS with Bearer-token authentication. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and enriched by the API Evangelist pipeline from public sources.

providers.name: Stllr Network
providers.description: Stllr Network is an AI-powered user-generated-content (UGC) and creator-marketing platform for the Arab world, connecting brands with a network of nano and micro content creators and influencers across categories such as beauty, entertainment, tech, lifestyle, parenting, gaming, fashion, fitness, and cooking. Its products include Remix, an AI tool that scales creator videos into multiple ad variations; Premier, a managed service that handles creator outreach and ad-campaign management; and pay-as-you-go video Packages (PAYG). The platform is brand- and consumer-facing, billed in Saudi Riyal (SAR), and sells through a fully published self-serve rate card of monthly UGC subscriptions and per-video bundles. It does not publish a public developer API, SDK, developer portal, or any API documentation: the string "API" does not appear anywhere on the marketing site. A real first-party backend does exist at api.stllr.network — the Next.js workspace at app.stllr.network calls its /v1/ routes, including TikTok and Google OAuth hand-offs — but it is an application backend with no published contract. Stllr has, by contrast, done deliberate agent-discovery work on its marketing surface: it serves a hand-written llms.txt and a robots.txt that explicitly allows OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, PerplexityBot, Claude-SearchBot, ClaudeBot and Google-Extended. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment.

providers.name: King Abdulaziz University
providers.description: King Abdulaziz University (KAU) is a large public research university in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, ranked #149 in the QS World University Rankings 2025, serving over 100,000 students across 33+ faculties and institutes. Its public web presence runs on the official kau.edu.sa (.gov.sa) domain and includes a beta "Open Data" page, a library/Deanship of Library Affairs portal, and a King Abdulaziz Scientific Platform. KAU operates gated identity infrastructure (an SSO portal at sso.kau.edu.sa and an Oracle Access Manager federation endpoint at iam.kau.edu.sa) but, as of this review, publishes no openly documented, self-service developer API, API reference, or developer portal. There is no official KAU GitHub organization; only a student-run Google Developer Student Club and individual academic projects are present on GitHub.

providers.name: King Saud University
providers.description: King Saud University (KSU) is a public research university in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, founded in 1957, and ranked #200 in the QS World University Rankings 2025. KSU operates a broad estate of digital services — including the Edugate student information system, an LMS, a library catalog, Saudi Digital Library access, a digitized manuscripts portal, and university e-services — but it does not publish a public, documented developer or API program. The systems found during review are end-user web applications gated behind institutional SSO/login rather than openly documented APIs. No public API reference, OpenAPI definition, developer portal, or open-data API endpoint could be confirmed.

providers.name: Johrh
providers.description: Johrh (جوهره للعبايات, "Johrh for Abayas") is a Saudi Arabian direct-to-consumer women's fashion retailer specializing in abayas, jalabiyas, niqabs, scarves (طرح), bags, and complementary modest-wear. The brand operates an Arabic-language online storefront hosted on the Zid e-commerce platform, selling across price tiers (99 SAR, 199 SAR, and premium occasion pieces) with checkout through Saudi payment and buy-now-pay-later gateways (Tabby, Tamara, Madfu, Emkan, ZidPay, Tap, MisPay). It was surfaced as a portfolio-linked company and added to the API Evangelist network; its public web surface is served by the Zid "Vitrin" storefront application, whose OpenAPI is published at johrh.com/openapi.json.

providers.name: Thamarah Al-Jill Co LLC
providers.description: Thamarah Al-Jill Co LLC operates AMUSED Co (amusedco.com), a Saudi Arabia-based online marketplace for authenticated, curated pre-loved luxury — designer handbags and women's clothing from houses such as Louis Vuitton, Hermes and Chanel at up to 70% off retail. Under a "Resell, Rebuy, Relove" model, buyers shop verified second-hand pieces (backed by a one-year authentication money-back guarantee) and sellers list their own unused items; payment options include credit card, Mada and Tamara. The store is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is built on Shopify and is fully agent-native: it publishes an /llms.txt agent guide and implements the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP) over an MCP endpoint, with Shopify Customer Accounts OpenID Connect for buyer authentication.

providers.name: Pemo
providers.description: Pemo is a UAE-based fintech offering smart corporate cards and an all-in-one spend management platform for businesses across the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia. The product combines physical and virtual corporate cards with expense management, automated receipt capture, invoice management, and accounting automation, giving finance teams real-time control and visibility over company spending. Pemo serves more than 10,000 companies and is backed by investors including Speedinvest. Pemo does not currently publish a public developer API or documentation portal; this profile tracks the company's identity and public web surface in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: SiFi
providers.description: SiFi (الحلول المبسطة المالية) is a Saudi Arabian fintech company offering a comprehensive corporate spend-management platform for businesses in the Kingdom. Licensed by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) and serving more than 5,000 clients, SiFi provides physical and virtual corporate cards with spending controls, real-time expense tracking, employee reimbursements, accounting automation, local vendor payments and international transfers (coming soon), and a cashback rewards program, delivered through web and iOS/Android mobile apps. SiFi is backed by QED Investors. No public developer API or documentation surface was found during this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Physiohome
providers.description: Physiohome, operating as Ameen (رعاية أمين), is a Saudi Arabia-based, tech-enabled provider of home rehabilitation and physical therapy services. Founded in 2021 out of a Ministry of Health sector accelerator, the company delivers physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy, nutritional therapy, and personal training for adults and seniors in patients' homes and rehabilitation centers. Its platform manages the full care journey from assessment and treatment planning through session tracking, provider equipping, and reporting, with 100+ active service providers operating across nine cities and a wider network of 700+ providers. Ameen offers iOS and Android apps, an online booking flow, and a patient portal, but publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal. It is a portfolio company of Sanabil 500 (500 Global) and Saudi Venture Capital.

providers.name: Speero
providers.description: Speero (سبيرو) is Saudi Arabia's online marketplace for authentic automotive spare parts, accessories, and professional vehicle services. The platform helps car owners find OEM and aftermarket parts for their specific make and model across all major categories (engine, brakes, suspension, lighting, AC, exhaust, and more) and book maintenance, detailing, paint and dent repair, tinting, and tire care at trusted workshops across the Kingdom. It supports browse-by-vehicle, installment payment options, and WhatsApp-based customer support. Speero is a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer marketplace and publishes no public developer API, but it does expose a machine-discovery surface (llms.txt, RFC 9116 security.txt, and an RFC 9727 api-catalog linkset).

providers.name: Ejari Co.
providers.description: Ejari (ايجاري) is a Riyadh-based property-technology and fintech company transforming the rental market in Saudi Arabia with a rent-now, pay-later (RNPL) model. Ejari pays a tenant's full annual rent to the landlord up front, then lets the tenant repay in twelve calm monthly installments, replacing the Kingdom's traditional single-cheque annual rent requirement. Founded in 2022 by Yazeed Al-Shamsi, Fahad Albedah, Mohammed Alkhelewy and Khalid Almunif, the company operates across 17+ Saudi cities and is building toward a full-service, Sharia-compliant real-estate super app. Ejari is backed by 500 Global and won the 2024 KPMG Global Tech Innovator competition.

providers.name: VOO (now SideUp)
providers.description: VOO was an Egyptian logistics marketplace that rebranded as SideUp in December 2022, relocating its headquarters to Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. SideUp is a fully integrated courier marketplace that lets e-commerce businesses ship locally and globally from one dashboard, connecting merchants with multiple courier services alongside payment gateways, shipping API integration, warehousing, and fulfillment, with plugins for Shopify, Salla, and OpenCart. Backed by 500 Global, Launch Africa VC, Riyadh Angels, and Alex Angels ($1.2M seed). No public developer portal or API documentation is published as of July 2026.

providers.name: Nqoodlet
providers.description: Nqoodlet is a Saudi Arabia-based (Riyadh) corporate spend and expense management platform for businesses from SMEs to enterprises. It lets teams issue unlimited virtual and physical company cards, track every transaction in real time, manage and control cards from a single dashboard, and pay globally in local currency without conversion fees. Over 600 companies use Nqoodlet to streamline expense management, eliminate paperwork, and gain clearer visibility into company spending. It is backed by 500 Global. Nqoodlet does not currently publish a public developer API, developer portal, SDKs, or API documentation; this profile captures the company's public web identity plus a live domain-security probe.

providers.name: Adalah for IT Systems LLC
providers.description: Adalah for IT Systems LLC operates Qanoniah, a Saudi Arabian legal technology platform that enables companies to access, understand, and act on the latest and most accurate legal information and procedures in seconds. The AI-driven service targets legal and compliance teams across Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, the company is tracked in the API Evangelist network; no public API or developer surface has been discovered to date.

providers.name: BRKZ
providers.description: BRKZ is a Saudi Arabian construction-technology company operating a B2B online marketplace for building materials and construction equipment. Positioned as a top online building materials store in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA), the platform connects contractors and construction businesses with material suppliers, streamlining procurement and offering nationwide delivery across Saudi Arabia. The bilingual (Arabic and English) storefront lets buyers source construction supplies online, and the company is backed by 500 Global among its investors. This profile was enriched from BRKZ's public web presence; the company runs a private, authenticated API host (api.brkz.com) but does not publish a public developer program, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: FIFOplus
providers.description: FIFOplus is a B2B smart-procurement marketplace for the HORECA sector (hotels, restaurants, cafes, and catering) in Saudi Arabia, connecting food-service buyers with suppliers across a webstore and mobile app that lists more than 5,000 food and non-food items spanning meat, seafood, dairy, produce, frozen goods, condiments, beverages, packaging, and cleaning supplies. The platform layers ordering, real-time order tracking, inventory, menu, and finance optimization with AI and integrates with point-of-sale systems and credit-terms payment. Founded in 2021 and headquartered in Jeddah, FIFOplus operates across Jeddah, Makkah, Riyadh, and Taif and is backed by the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator (500 Global) and Palm Ventures. This profile is maintained by the API Evangelist network; FIFOplus publishes no public developer API, OpenAPI, or developer portal at this time.

providers.name: Gathern
providers.description: Gathern (جاذر) is the first licensed peer-to-peer vacation-rental marketplace in Saudi Arabia, founded in Riyadh in 2016 and licensed by the Saudi Ministry of Tourism. Through its iOS, Android, and web apps, travelers book short-term private accommodations directly from local hosts — chalets, apartments, villas, farms, resorts, rest houses (istrahat), camps, caravans, and rooms — across more than 200 cities and provinces in the Kingdom, including Riyadh, Jeddah, Taif, Al Khobar, Dammam, Mecca, Medina, and AlUla. The platform lists tens of thousands of units, has served more than five million users, and holds a leading share of the alternative-hospitality sector in Saudi Arabia. Backed by 500 Global, STV, Sanabil Investments (a Public Investment Fund subsidiary), and others, Gathern raised a $72M Series B and is preparing for a Tadawul listing. Gathern operates as a consumer marketplace app and does not currently publish a public developer API surface; this profile tracks its public web properties for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Sabbar
providers.description: Sabbar is a leading local employment and recruitment platform in Saudi Arabia that connects job seekers with employers across many sectors. Job seekers search listings, build a free CV, and apply to roles, while employers use subscription-based recruitment packages and candidate matching. The platform reports more than 12,000 companies and over 1 million Saudi and non-Saudi job seekers, with iOS and Android mobile apps. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. No public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: Safqah Holdings Limited
providers.description: Safqah Holdings Limited operates Safqah (Safqah Capital / Safqah Financial), a Saudi Arabian fintech platform headquartered in the Al-Malqa district of Riyadh and regulated by the Saudi Capital Market Authority (CMA). Safqah provides Sharia-compliant, debt-based real estate investment opportunities that let qualified individual and institutional investors fund real estate development deals starting from 1,000 SAR, alongside a financing arm that offers land acquisition, residential development, commercial development, raw land, and bridge financing to real estate developers. Investors track deal performance through periodic reporting and live project camera feeds. The platform is a consumer- and investor-facing web application with no publicly documented developer API, SDK, or integration surface at this time.

providers.name: Awfar Market
providers.description: Awfar is a Cairo- and Riyadh-based digital solutions company (founded 2013) offering an integrated customer engagement and commerce platform. It combines an omnichannel Chat Center with AI agents (WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook), a cloud Call Center, and a Commerce & Delivery platform for order, inventory, and logistics management within a single interface. Awfar serves more than 2,000 clients across retail, pharmacy, restaurant, e-commerce, tourism, healthcare, education, and real estate, and ships prebuilt integrations for Shopify, Meta, Odoo, Zid, and Salla plus custom API connections. Backed by 500 Global. No public developer portal or OpenAPI specification is published at this time; integration is arranged via the sales and demo channel.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Barakah
providers.description: Barakah is a Saudi foodtech company operating a consumer mobile marketplace that fights food waste by connecting restaurants, cafes, hotels, bakeries, and grocery retailers with consumers who buy their surplus, still-fresh meals and food products at discounts of up to 70 percent for pickup or delivery. Founded in Jeddah and backed by 500 Global, FoodLabs, and Salica Investments, Barakah has grown into one of the most downloaded food and drink apps in Saudi Arabia with partnerships across more than 800 merchants, including global brands. Barakah is a business-to-consumer mobile application and does not currently publish a public developer platform, API, or SDK; this profile captures its identity and public web surface.

providers.name: Emtethal
providers.description: Emtethal is a Riyadh, Saudi Arabia based smart compliance and inspection management platform for the food service and hospitality sectors, backed by 500 Global. The platform automates inspection scheduling and distribution, provides custom checklists per facility type, captures photo documentation with automatic timestamps and GPS location, detects and categorizes violations automatically, and pushes real-time alerts for critical issues. It layers analytics and compliance reporting on top of an offline-capable mobile field-inspection app (iOS and Android) and AI-powered camera and sensor monitoring. Emtethal serves both individual food facilities and consulting firms managing multiple client sites, offering a 14-day free trial. There is no public API, developer portal, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile is an API Evangelist company lead maintained for enrichment and monitoring.

providers.name: Siolla
providers.description: Siolla is a Saudi financial-technology company offering a consumer investment-management mobile application. It provides professionally managed, fully Sharia-compliant investment portfolios, an in-app academy and educational resources covering financial fundamentals, budgeting and investment strategy, and simplified access to investing for modern investors. Siolla is licensed and regulated by the Saudi Capital Market Authority. The company presents a consumer app and website only; no public developer program, API, or developer documentation is published at this time.

providers.name: Happy World
providers.description: Happy World operates SPICE (getspice.com), a premium lifestyle dining and rewards mobile application based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. SPICE lets diners discover curated partner restaurants across the Kingdom, reserve or walk in, pay their bill in-app by entering the bill number, and earn instant cashback rewards (advertised as up to 20% cashback with no caps) on every visit. The product emphasizes intelligent personalization and a hand-picked selection of the best restaurants, food, and dining experiences. Surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network. The company is a consumer mobile-app business with no public API, developer portal, SDKs, or documented developer surface at this time; this profile captures its identity and public web properties.

providers.name: Drahim Holdings
providers.description: Drahim (دراهم) is a Saudi personal-finance and automated-investment fintech, founded in Riyadh in 2021 by Sultan Alkhayal and Yasser Alshurihi. Its mobile app uses open banking to aggregate a user's bank accounts into one view, enriches and auto-categorizes transactions (2.5B+ processed), and offers auto-savings, Zakat calculation, and Sharia-compliant robo-advisory portfolios spanning 40+ funds across Saudi and global equities, real estate, and commodities. Drahim is licensed by the Saudi Central Bank (SAMA) for open-banking/payment services and by the Capital Market Authority (CMA) for investment management; it was backed by Y Combinator and 500 Global, and Al Rajhi Bank acquired a 65% majority stake in 2024. Drahim is a consumer application and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal; this profile captures its corporate and product identity plus live domain-security posture. Consumer surfaces include the iOS and Android apps and a business platform.

providers.name: Salasa
providers.description: Salasa is an end-to-end eCommerce logistics provider based in Saudi Arabia, offering 3PL fulfillment (warehouse storage, automated pick/pack/ship), hyperlocal dark stores with 2-hour delivery in Riyadh, domestic on-demand and scheduled shipping, cross-border shipping with customs clearance, and reverse logistics / return management. Its Operations Management System (OMS) provides real-time tracking, inventory management, and analytics, and it connects to major eCommerce platforms (Salla, Zid, Shopify, WooCommerce, Magento, Amazon, Trendyol) and offers custom API integrations for merchants automating fulfillment and order synchronization.

providers.name: Juleb
providers.description: Juleb is a Saudi Arabia-based pharma-tech and retail software company providing an integrated cloud platform for the health, retail, and distribution sectors. Its suite spans accounting and financial management, inventory and warehouse management, sales force automation (SFA), point of sale (POS), Rx e-prescription, e-commerce, and DSCSA regulatory compliance. Juleb connects to Saudi compliance systems (ZATCA/Fatoora, RSD, GS1, Wasfaty), e-commerce channels (Salla, Shopify, HungerStation), payment providers (Geidea, Alhamrani), and ERPs (Microsoft Dynamics). Founded by Yousuf Jamjoom and backed by 500 Global, Juleb exposes a REST API (documented at docs.juleb.com) covering inventory, point of sale, prescriptions, and partner/company resources.

providers.name: Erad
providers.description: Erad is a licensed, Sharia-compliant fintech lender providing fast, flexible working capital to small and medium-sized businesses across Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates. Founded in 2022 (Y Combinator S22) and headquartered in Riyadh, Erad offers revenue-based financing, invoice financing (advancing up to 90% of B2B/B2G invoices in as little as 48 hours), and supplier financing to revenue-generating SMEs. The company embeds working-capital products into supplier networks and business platforms, and is backed by investors including Y Combinator, 500 Global, Nuwa Capital, Khwarizmi Ventures, Aljazira Capital, VentureSouq, Oraseya Capital and Joa Capital, alongside debt facilities from Stride Ventures and a $125M asset-backed facility led by Jefferies with Channel Capital.

providers.name: CarSwitch
providers.description: CarSwitch is a tech-enabled used-car marketplace founded in Dubai in 2016 that facilitates buying and selling of pre-owned vehicles across the United Arab Emirates (Dubai, Abu Dhabi and nationwide) and Saudi Arabia. Rather than a traditional classifieds site, CarSwitch operates as a fully managed service: every car undergoes a 200-point inspection before listing, sellers get an end-to-end managed selling service (professional photography, listing, negotiation and RTA transfer handling), and buyers get price transparency, a free online car-valuation tool and installment financing through banking partners such as Emirates NBD, FAB, ADCB, ADIB, DIB and Emirates Islamic. The company has inspected 130,000+ vehicles and facilitated over $500 million in sales. CarSwitch was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network; it is a consumer marketplace with no public developer API program.

providers.name: Sweater
providers.description: Sweater (سويتر) is a Saudi Arabian on-demand mobile car-care company that brings waterless vehicle washing, interior cleaning, detailing, and fragrance services to customers wherever their car is parked. Its app-based platform uses smart scheduling to dispatch field teams by location and uses roughly 7 liters of water per wash versus about 120 liters for traditional methods. The company reports 2M+ washes, 750K+ users, 500+ corporate partnerships, and operations across 8 Saudi cities (Riyadh, Dammam, Khobar, Jeddah, Jubail, Medina, Al-Hassa, and Mecca). Surfaced as a 500 Global portfolio company. It is a consumer/B2B services business with no public developer API surface at this time.

providers.name: Telgani
providers.description: Telgani is an app-based car rental aggregator founded in 2018 and headquartered in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Its consumer iOS and Android apps let users compare prices and book cars from more than 50 partner rental companies with over 500 branches across the Kingdom, offering doorstep delivery, airport pickup, and daily, monthly, or yearly rentals. Backed by 500 Global, Impact46, and Elm, Telgani has raised roughly $8.5M across a seed round, a 2021 pre-Series A, and a 2023 Series A. Telgani operates as a consumer mobile marketplace and does not publish a public developer API program; this profile captures its public web properties (homepage, privacy policy, terms of service) and its domain security posture.

providers.name: DailyMealz
providers.description: DailyMealz is a Saudi Arabia-based meal subscription service that delivers fresh daily lunches and full-day meal plans sourced from a network of more than sixty partner restaurants. Subscribers choose a package (healthy, keto, diet, and similar options), select meals from a rotating menu, and control delivery timing through the DailyMealz mobile app. The company also operates a DailyMealz for Business offering for corporate meal programs. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment; DailyMealz is an app-first consumer brand and publishes no public developer API surface, documentation portal, or API specifications as of this profiling round.

providers.name: Quantum
providers.description: Quantum is a Saudi Arabian advertising-technology (adtech) enabler that bridges online publishers and advertisers with data and technology. Its Quantum One omnichannel platform connects online and offline retail experiences across programmatic ads, in-app media buying, e-sampling, on-ground activations, influencer marketing, and out-of-home media, with goal-attainment tracking, ROI measurement, customer-engagement analytics, and conversion-rate analysis. As of this enrichment pass the company publishes no public developer API, documentation, or developer portal; the Quantum One tenant application does carry an API-key management screen, so the platform issues keys to signed-in customers, but no contract, reference, or machine-readable spec is published anywhere.

providers.name: Ajeer
providers.description: Ajeer (iajeer.com) is a Saudi Arabian on-demand services platform for home and facility maintenance and operations (خدمات الصيانة والتشغيل). Through its mobile application customers request residential maintenance, general labor, installation, plumbing, electrical, and air-conditioning services, connecting them with vetted service providers. Ajeer is a portfolio company of 500 Global, surfaced into the API Evangelist network as a company profile. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found during enrichment; this profile captures the company's public web surface and domain-security posture.

providers.name: MisMar
providers.description: MisMar (مسمار) is a Saudi Arabian automotive maintenance and repair platform that connects vehicle owners with certified service centers. It runs a consumer mobile app (B2C) alongside a Network-as-a-Service (NaaS) platform and Workshop Management System (WMS) that digitize fleet management, order processing, and workshop operations for business (B2B), government (B2G), and insurance partners. Services span fault diagnostics, accident restoration, oil and battery and tire changes, periodic maintenance, car wash, and protective treatments across 45+ Saudi cities, with at-home or center-based delivery and warranty coverage. MisMar is a portfolio company of 500 Global. No public developer API, OpenAPI, or SDK surface is currently published.

providers.name: Behja
providers.description: Behja (Behja Holdings Limited Inc) is a licensed real estate platform in Saudi Arabia (License 120022677) that offers flexible rental-to-own housing. Its model lets residents select a property, apply, sign a three-year lease, and then buy with a full year's rent credited back toward the purchase. The integrated platform handles leases, purchases, and utility payments in one place. Behja is a portfolio company of 500 Global and was added to the API Evangelist network as a company profile; it does not currently publish a public developer program, API, SDKs, or technical documentation.

providers.name: ElMetr
providers.description: ElMetr (المتر) is a Middle East legal-tech company providing online legal consultation and guidance for companies, entrepreneurs, and individuals. The platform combines licensed lawyers with modern technology to connect users with qualified legal help, offering subscription legal packages that cover company formation and registration, contract review, compliance, intellectual property, and dispute resolution. Founded in Egypt and now operating in Saudi Arabia, ElMetr aims to make legal work clear, fast, and fair so businesses can move faster and reduce risk from first idea through expansion. ElMetr is a 500 Global (500 Startups) portfolio company. This company profile has been through the API Evangelist enrichment pipeline; ElMetr does not currently publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD
providers.description: EQUIPTAL HOLDING LTD operates Moedatech (معداتك), Saudi Arabia's first digital procurement and rental marketplace for heavy construction equipment, connecting contractors with verified suppliers of excavators, cranes, and trucks through RFQs, real-time bidding, and audit-ready digital contracts. Founded in Riyadh in 2020 by Ali Merie and Mansour Hmaid, the company pairs the marketplace with a telematics/fleet layer (built on Traccar GPS tracking) so equipment owners can monitor real-time asset performance. The product ships as iOS and Android apps plus a web app; there is no publicly documented developer API at this time. The company is backed by 500 Global and Plug and Play Middle East. This profile was surfaced from the 500 Global portfolio and enriched from the company's public web, brand (moedatech.net), and GitHub presence.

providers.name: Trella
providers.description: Trella is a Cairo-headquartered B2B trucking marketplace and digital freight platform that connects shippers with carriers across the Middle East, North Africa, and Pakistan (MENA-P). Founded in 2019 by Omar Hagrass, Ali El Atrash, and Pierre Saad and backed by Y Combinator, Trella runs a digital load marketplace, a carrier mobile app, and a shipper web dashboard that together replace the traditional broker-driven, paper-based long-haul trucking workflow. Core platform services include load posting and carrier matching, instant quoting, GPS tracking and live shipment visibility, electronic proof of delivery (ePODs), load insurance, a control-tower operations layer for carrier quality and performance, and integrated payments and invoicing between shippers and carriers. The network spans 30,000+ carriers and operates from major freight hubs including Cairo, Alexandria, Port Said, Damietta, Sokhna, Jeddah, Dammam, Riyadh, and Dubai, serving industries such as FMCG, construction, manufacturing, agriculture, mining, e-commerce, retail, electronics, ceramics, and freight forwarding. Trella's revenue model is marketplace take-rate and value-added logistics services; there is no public developer API, SDK, OpenAPI specification, webhooks catalog, or open-source platform release for the Trella marketplace.

providers.name: Governata
providers.description: Governata is a Saudi Arabia-based data governance and management platform that helps government entities and enterprises turn complex data into business value through comprehensive, PDPL-aligned data management. Its product suite spans Data Governance (business glossary, data catalog, data classification, data lineage, metadata store, data quality), Master Data Management (domains, golden record, matching and survivorship), Data Privacy (personal-data discovery and protection under Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law, access management, and a service catalog), and Governata Core, an administrative backbone covering license management, audit trail, and workflows. Governata packages role-based solutions for chief data officers, compliance officers, data protection officers, and data stewards, and sector solutions for government, healthcare, financial services, insurance, telecom, retail, energy, and large enterprises. It is backed by 500 Global and is being profiled in the API Evangelist network. No public API, developer portal, or machine-readable specification was found at the time of enrichment; this profile captures the company's identity and web presence.

providers.name: Desaisiv Inc.
providers.description: DESAISIV is a corporate InsurTech platform focused on health insurance in Saudi Arabia and the wider MENA region. Founded in 2022, the company builds AI and automation products for insurers and third-party administrators (TPAs), including smart underwriting automation, a real-time quotation engine, OCR-powered claims intelligence, a corporates insurance marketplace, and SME portals. Its platform bridges data, systems, insurers, and corporates to streamline underwriting, quoting, and claims. DESAISIV is backed by 500 Global, Terra VC, Oqal, and other MENA/UK/US investors via a US$2M pre-seed round. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; the company does not currently publish a public developer portal or API.

providers.name: Autobia
providers.description: Autobia is a B2B e-commerce marketplace for the automotive aftermarket in Saudi Arabia, connecting auto-parts retailers, workshops, and service centers with wholesalers and dealers. The platform offers real-time pricing and instant ordering across more than 20,000 spare parts from multiple brands, centralizing sourcing to streamline procurement and improve supply-chain efficiency for the automotive sector. Backed by Techstars, Autobia operates via a web platform and native iOS and Android apps. No public developer API, documentation, or SDK is currently published.

providers.name: Esar
providers.description: Esar (ايسار) is a Saudi Arabia and UAE based car rental marketplace that connects vehicle owners with renters through a mobile app, offering luxury, sports, family, and 4x4 vehicles across Riyadh, Jeddah, Mecca, and Dubai. The platform lets car owners list vehicles to earn recurring returns while giving travelers on-demand access to a curated fleet at competitive daily rates. Headquartered in Jeddah, Esar is an early-stage startup backed by 500 Global and the Taqadam accelerator. This API Evangelist profile tracks the company as a portfolio lead; no public developer API surface has been found to date.

providers.name: Haseel
providers.description: Haseel (حصيل) is a Riyadh-based technology startup, founded in 2018, that delivers fresh fruits and vegetables to consumers across Saudi Arabia through its iOS and Android mobile apps. The company sources high-quality produce and fulfills each order from the nearest of its branches inside Riyadh, pairing a curated selection with fast, reliable last-mile delivery. Haseel reports more than 400,000 app downloads, three branches inside Riyadh, and over 1,000 orders per day, and is backed by 500 Global. This profile is maintained in the API Evangelist network; Haseel is a consumer produce-delivery app and does not currently publish a public developer API or OpenAPI surface.

providers.name: Tammwel
providers.description: Tammwel (Tamawal) is a Saudi Arabian digital financing intermediary that connects consumers with licensed financial institutions to compare and obtain Sharia-compliant financing. Its consumer platform and iOS/Android apps let users apply once and receive multiple offers across four products - personal loans, credit cards, auto financing, and mortgage financing (each up to 150,000 SAR) - emphasizing transparent pricing with no hidden fees. The company is a portfolio company of 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass Tammwel publishes no public API, developer portal, documentation, SDK, or /.well-known discovery surface; this profile captures its identity and infrastructure security posture.

providers.name: Doos
providers.description: Doos is a Saudi-based quick-commerce (q-commerce) platform and mobile app that delivers groceries, fresh produce, beauty, gifting, pharmacy, and lifestyle products in minutes across Saudi Arabia. Founded in 2023 by Tala Al Sahsah, it operates cloud/dark stores in Jeddah and Riyadh with localised assortments, prices, and promotions by city and delivery zone, offering a bilingual (Arabic/English) shopping experience. Doos is backed by 500 Global and received a strategic investment from Jahez to accelerate its expansion in the Kingdom's growing quick-commerce sector. This is a consumer-facing storefront; no public developer program or API has been identified at this time.

providers.name: Noon
providers.description: Noon is a Dubai-headquartered e-commerce marketplace and digital ecosystem launched in 2017 as a joint venture between Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Emirati businessman Mohamed Alabbar. Frequently described as the Amazon of the MENA region, Noon operates as the leading online shopping destination across the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, and Egypt, offering electronics, mobiles, fashion, beauty, home, appliances, baby, and grocery categories through a hybrid first-party and third-party seller marketplace. Beyond the core marketplace, Noon has expanded into a lifestyle super-app spanning Noon Food (quick-service restaurant delivery competing with Talabat and Deliveroo), Noon Daily (next-day grocery delivery), Noon Minutes (15-minute instant grocery and essentials delivery), Noon Pay and the Noon mobile wallet (QR payments, bill pay, and a co-branded credit card), Noon VIP (loyalty/subscription), NowNow (on-demand delivery in KSA), and SIVVI (acquired regional fashion brand). Noon operates its own last-mile logistics arm and warehouses across the region, and provides a Fulfilled by Partner Integration (FBPI) program with commercial APIs that allow third-party sellers and channel-integration partners (ChannelEngine, Unicommerce, Vinculum, Ecom Energize and others) to programmatically publish catalog, sync inventory, and manage shipments. These APIs are gated to onboarded sellers and certified integrators inside the noon.partners environment — there is no general public developer portal, no published OpenAPI specification, and no Noon-maintained SDKs, CLIs, or open-source repositories.

providers.name: Sanad Cash
providers.description: Sanad Cash was a Saudi Arabia-based fintech startup that operated an on-demand payment platform, giving employees early access to earned wages and providing employers with tools to manage on-demand pay. The company raised a $1.6M seed round in January 2022 with participation from Impact46 and was backed by 500 Global. Sanad Cash was acquired by HyperPay in July 2023, and the Sanad Cash business was subsequently acquired by Qashio in October 2025. The independent sanadcash.com property is no longer reachable (no live HTTPS service), so this profile documents the company's identity and residual domain footprint rather than a live developer/API surface.

providers.name: UTURN
providers.description: UTURN Entertainment is a Saudi Arabian digital media and entertainment company founded in 2010 that has grown into the largest Arabic Multi-Channel Network (MCN) in the MENA region. It produces original digital content — comedy sketches, gaming (Saudi Gamer), women's lifestyle (Unseen), sports (MLM), and MMA (MMAnia) shows — distributed across YouTube, TikTok, Snapchat, and other social platforms, and offers content creation, sponsored content, branded content, and digital production services to brands. A 500 Global portfolio company, UTURN publishes no public API or developer surface.

providers.name: Melon Digital Insurance
providers.description: Melon is a digital-first insurance agency based in Saudi Arabia, building modern Insurtech products for individuals across the Kingdom. The company has received preliminary approval from the Saudi Insurance Authority (IA) to operate as a digital insurance agency, with final licensing pending, and is currently pre-launch ("launching soon"). Melon uses technology and AI to deliver transparent, fair pricing, simple policies, and a seamless, fully digital customer experience. It is backed by 500 Global. As of this enrichment pass, Melon publishes only a marketing landing page (melon.sa) with no public developer portal, API documentation, or machine-readable API surface.

providers.name: Firnas Aero
providers.description: Firnas Aero is a Saudi Arabian deep-tech startup building autonomous Drone-in-a-Box (DiaB) systems for aerial surveillance, industrial inspection, and environmental assessment. Its turnkey platform pairs self-charging, robotic battery-swapping drone stations with cloud-based remote management over 5G, Ethernet, or Wi-Fi, and applies machine-learning and deep-learning models for anomaly detection, Foreign Object Debris (FOD) detection, hazard identification, and geo-location. Based at KRTP HQ in Thuwal, Saudi Arabia, the company serves infrastructure, energy, and security clients including Red Sea Global, NEOM, and the Saudi Electricity Company, and is backed by 500 Global. It is tracked in the API Evangelist network as a company profile; no public developer API surface was found during enrichment.

providers.name: MEDICAL INTELLIGENCE CO
providers.description: Medicarri (operated by Medical Intelligence Co) is a B2B healthtech marketplace based in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia that connects clinics and healthcare facilities with medical suppliers, letting buyers source medical supplies and equipment from many vendors in one place. The company was selected for Batch 4 of the Sanabil 500 MENA Seed Accelerator Program run by 500 Global and Sanabil Investments. As of this profile Medicarri operates a customer-facing e-commerce web application at medicarri.com and does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI specification, or developer portal.

providers.name: Alwans
providers.description: Alwans is a Saudi technology investment and startup-development company based in Al Khubar, Saudi Arabia, and launched in January 2010. The firm is focused on enriching local Arabic technical content and competing globally by investing in and building startup ideas and technology projects, with an emphasis on e-commerce, online marketing, mobile applications, and mobile games. Alwans is a small team (2-10 employees) and is itself backed by 500 Global; its portfolio includes companies such as Foodics and Fnjalah. It publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDKs -- this profile is an identity record within the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: FAI & GLOBAL SOLUTIONS HOLDING LIMITED
providers.description: FAI & GLOBAL SOLUTIONS HOLDING LIMITED is a Saudi Arabian holding company surfaced as a portfolio company of 500 Global and added to the API Evangelist network for enrichment. Its site at fai.sa is a WordPress property served from nginx behind a WAF that returns HTTP 403 to every external request except /robots.txt, so no company description, developer portal, documentation, or API surface could be retrieved during the enrichment pass. No public API, specification, SDK, or event surface has been observed to date; the domain-security posture was probed successfully and is recorded in security/. Re-probe from an allowed network on a later round to confirm whether a developer surface exists behind the block.
